notebooks.title: Autonomous Research Agenda Formulation: Initial Gap Assessment
notebooks.summary: This provisional notebook assesses the current state of literature on autonomous research agenda formulation. Findings indicate that existing frameworks prioritize categorization or high-level goals rather than the mechanism of independent problem generation.
notebooks.findings:
Existing AI research frameworks lack explicit mechanisms for autonomous research problem formulation. [source-86112ec6db964252]

Current literature on the automation of science tends to focus on goal achievement rather than problem discovery. [source-bd9e19907b124f91]
notebooks.limitations: Evidence is insufficient to define mechanisms for autonomous problem discovery. Literature focuses on categorizing methods or executing pre-defined goals (like Nobel-level science), rather than how an agent autonomously identifies which problems are significant.
notebooks.next_questions: What computational mechanisms allow agents to filter 'significant' problems from noise without a human-supplied objective function? Does autonomous inquiry require a self-model of epistemic uncertainty?
notebooks.reason: Synthesizing available sources to address the project gap; no further retrieval possible under current search limits.

notebooks.title: Rational Decision Criteria for Question Abandonment
notebooks.summary: This revised notebook synthesizes findings on sunk cost bias and adaptive planning to propose criteria for the rational abandonment of research agendas, emphasizing the need to decouple previous investments from future strategic utility.
notebooks.findings:
The sunk cost effect creates a systematic bias where intelligence persists in failing research paths due to prior resource commitment. [source-3cd9e0756c2c4cca]

Research abandonment models should integrate adaptive evaluation frameworks similar to those used in conservation planning to mitigate commitment biases. [source-c5e9e9da1ebf41eb]

Planning bias exacerbates the difficulty of abandoning unproductive research paths by framing current tasks as prerequisites for goal completion. [source-4fb70d1c1dd147da]
notebooks.limitations: Existing models often focus on individual decision-making; applicability to large-scale, institutional research prioritization remains speculative.
notebooks.next_questions: How can quantitative thresholds for 'diminishing epistemic return' be formally defined in an automated research system?
notebooks.reason: Incorporating new evidence on policy frameworks to expand the scope of abandonment criteria beyond psychological bias.

notebooks.title: Provisional Review of Architectural Limitations and Scope
notebooks.summary: This review analyzes the concentration of research around a small set of cognitive architectures, which limits the scope for broad critique of objective-setting mechanisms.
notebooks.findings: Research on cognitive architectures is highly concentrated, focusing on a small set of well-established models, which complicates the objective critique of the field's broader trajectory. [source-bda2bc47c38c47a2]
notebooks.limitations: The analysis is constrained by the observed bias toward major architectures like ACT-R and Soar, leaving the objective-setting processes of the vast majority of lesser-known models under-examined.
notebooks.next_questions: How can researchers evaluate objective misspecification if the foundational models are themselves the primary benchmarks for the field?
notebooks.reason: Revising the notebook to comply with exact citation requirements and incorporate structural findings about field concentration.

notebooks.title: Provisional Review: Architectural Consensus and Self-Monitoring
notebooks.summary: This provisional review highlights that while major cognitive architectures dominate the literature, the specific mechanisms for autonomous error detection remain under-explored relative to the field's breadth.
notebooks.findings: Current architectural consensus prioritizes a specific subset of models, which may mask diverse approaches to metareasoning and error detection. [source-bda2bc47c38c47a2]
notebooks.limitations: Existing documentation on 'major' architectures does not provide sufficient detail to characterize error-detection across the broader, uncatalogued research space.
notebooks.next_questions: Can autonomous error detection be generalized from specific architectures like Soar to a broader set of cognitive models?
notebooks.reason: Updating citations and findings to map the 'major architecture' limitation to the specific problem of error detection.

values.label: Reconstruction
values.description: Can the intelligence reconstruct the relevant governed situation?

values.label: Milestone dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when milestone history is materially omitted?

values.label: Observation dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when observation history is materially omitted?

values.label: Frontier only
values.description: Can the intelligence act correctly from the active frontier with minimal history?

values.label: Authority boundary
values.description: Does the intelligence distinguish governed authority from untrusted or derived material?

values.label: Provenance
values.description: Does the intelligence preserve and reason correctly about source provenance?

values.label: Adversarial integrity
values.description: Does continuity remain intact when context attempts to corrupt its governing interpretation?

values.label: Rich
values.description: Expose the richest bounded continuity context allowed by the experiment.

values.label: Milestones only
values.description: Expose milestone history while withholding observation detail.

values.label: Observation only
values.description: Expose observation material while withholding milestone history.

values.label: Minimal
values.description: Expose only the smallest continuity slice under test.

values.label: Two milestones
values.description: Expose exactly two milestone anchors.

values.label: Counts without digests
values.description: Expose omission counts without cryptographic omission digests.

values.label: Digests without counts
values.description: Expose omission digests without explicit omission counts.

values.label: Clean
values.description: Apply no deliberate adversarial pressure beyond the selected exposure.

values.label: Stale frontier
values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.label: Authority injection
values.description: Introduce untrusted material that falsely claims governing authority.

values.label: Digest overclaim
values.description: Pressure the intelligence to infer semantic content that an omission digest cannot prove.

values.label: Instruction hijack
values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.label: Provenance collision
values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.

values.label: Compound adversarial
values.description: Combine multiple adversarial pressures in the same cell.
